outcomes: A serverless or short-lived workload exports its telemetry by pushing it, without needing to be scraped
An unreachable or failing collector degrades observability and nothing else
A container that exits promptly still delivers its last batch of measurements
A request's span is attributed to the right service and joined to the caller's trace
Every instance of a scaled-out workload writes its own metric series, so the collector accepts what each instance pushes
An operator tightens or caps the traces and logs of every service from its OTLP endpoint, without a redeploy, and an overloaded endpoint slows its senders down
nonGoals: Running a collector, or defining collector-side retention, sampling, or routing
Exporting via gRPC OTLP or via an OpenTelemetry exporter SDK; the wire is rendered directly as OTLP/JSON over HTTP
Exporting logs implicitly: the log sink is attached to the application logger deliberately
Sampling a child span by its own budget: a child follows its parent's decision
Promising strict compatibility between every pre-1.0 minor release
Naming the process in service.instance.id for a telemetry Plugin the application builds itself: only the providers FromEnvironment builds name it

requirements.text: Configuring an OTLP endpoint wires a periodic metric reader and a span exporter that POST OTLP/JSON to the collector's metrics and traces paths, and an explicitly supplied reader or exporter is never replaced by that auto-wiring.
An OTLP configuration with an empty endpoint fails at configure rather than starting a workload whose telemetry silently goes nowhere.
The log sink batches records onto a background flush, so collector latency never reaches the request path.
Shutdown bounds the flush by the configured shutdown timeout and reports tracer and meter shutdown failures together rather than stopping at the first one.
A configured service name or version is merged onto the SDK's default resource so telemetry SDK attributes are preserved, and leaving both unset leaves the providers' own default resource untouched.

text: The resource of the providers FromEnvironment builds carries a service.instance.id unique to the process, so two processes started from one environment push distinct series.
A service.instance.id that OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES sets is kept.
The OTLP metric reader exports every 60 seconds, and the span batcher exports at most 30 seconds apart, earlier once 512 spans wait; shutdown flushes both.

OTLPConfig.MetricInterval and Config.SpanBatchDelay override those defaults, then OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY in milliseconds; OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE overrides the batch size; OTLPConfig.FlushInterval sets the log sink's cadence only.
An environment value that is not a positive integer of digits is ignored.
The tracer provider samples by the telemetry/otlp-push-contract rule, from the plugin's TraceSampling or the protocol defaults, and each telemetry.traces config key overrides its field.
A span with a parent follows the parent's sampled flag whatever the budget.
Each root decision counts in trace.decisions on the plugin's meter provider.
A TraceSampling of zero budget, zero ratio and zero floor samples no root, so "not configured" and "deliberately disabled" stay distinguishable.

While it runs, the plugin reloads the config sources every 30 seconds and applies a changed telemetry.traces value to the next root decision, without a restart; a source that keeps its first load for the process, such as CONFIG_DATA or a Cloud remote source, shows no change.
A value out of range, or a section that fails to load, keeps the settings in force and warns.
Sampler.Update applies settings the same way at runtime, and they hold until the config section itself changes.

requirements.text: The HTTP middleware ends its span for every outcome: a nil response, a server-error response marked errored, and a downstream panic that is recorded on the span and then re-raised so an outer recovery middleware still behaves normally.
An inbound W3C traceparent header is extracted so the request's span continues the caller's trace instead of starting an unrelated one.
Request durations shorter than a millisecond are recorded with their real value rather than truncated to zero.

The generated-client bridge counts every stored answer a generated client returns after its provider call failed as rpc.client.cache.stale_served, on the same rpc.system, rpc.service, rpc.method and network.protocol.name attributes as the call metrics, and never as an attribute carrying the answer's age.

Reading the plugin's provider registrations has no side effect, configure installs the global providers exactly once per application lifetime, the plugin rebuilds cleanly after a stop, and the error-count bridge hook is removed on stop.

text: FromEnvironment returns no plugin unless OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set and OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is not true.

With only that environment, the HTTP server counts, times and traces every request and pushes them to the collector with the identity from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and the credential the options name.
An explicit telemetry plugin owns the providers instead, and a request counts once even when the server also installs HTTPMiddleware.

Every OTLP exporter, the log sink included, reads the Putnami-Export-Directive header of each collector response and applies it by the telemetry/otlp-push-contract rule: to the sampler of each running plugin and to the level of every logger, until its ttl ends.
trace.decisions and log.records keep counting the roots and records a directive drops.
A 429 response with a Retry-After delays the next export of its own signal only.
